text: What is the Capabilities Approach CA. <break time="0.8s" /> And why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it. <break time="0.8s" /> It is easy to say what it is not. <break time="0.8s" /> The CA does not rank animals. <break time="0.8s" /> By likeness to humans. <break time="0.8s" /> Or seek special privileges. <break time="0.8s" /> For those considered most like us. <break time="0.8s" /> As do some other popular theoretical approaches. <break time="0.8s" /> The CA has concern for the finch and the pig. <break time="0.8s" /> As much as the whale and the elephant. <break time="0.8s" /> And it argues. <break time="0.8s" /> That the human form of life is simply irrelevant. <break time="0.8s" /> When we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves. <break time="0.8s" /> What is relevant is their own forms of life. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy. <break time="0.8s" /> The characteristic goods of a human life. <break time="0.8s" /> So a finch seeks a finchs life. <break time="0.8s" /> And the whale a whales life. <break time="0.8s" /> We should extend ourselves and learn. <break time="0.8s" /> Not lazily picture animals as lesser humans. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeking a life sort of like our own. <break time="0.8s" /> According to the CA. <break time="0.8s" /> Each sentient creature should have the opportunity. <break time="0.8s" /> To flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.
